source.title: Interpreting Neural Networks through the Polytope Lens
source.authors: Sid Black; Lee D. Sharkey; Léo Grinsztajn; Eric Winsor; Daniel A. Braun; Jacob Merizian; Kip Parker; Carlos Ram'on Guevara; Beren Millidge; Gabriel Alfour; Connor Leahy

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses superposition and polysemanticity but its own experiments test polytope-lens predictions, not the listed versions of the superposition claim.
record.gate_note: The paper reports experiments on activation and spline-code clusters, polytope-boundary density, and scaling activation vectors. These results concern semantic organization by polytopes, a related but different construct from the named claim versions, so they are recorded with versions ["none"]. Its discussion of superposition and directions is conceptual and partly cites earlier work.
record.test_reason: The experiments test the authors' own polytope-lens predictions: activation and spline-code clusters are monosemantic, polytope density is higher between classes, and density marks where scaled directions break. Superposition appears only as motivation and in conceptual discussion. The paper argues that a sparse overcomplete basis is insufficient without accounting for nonlinearity, but gives no result on any version. The NMF-vs-neuron comparison in GPT2-small layer 4 (r3) comes closest to V4. It is qualitative and uses 64 non-overcomplete NMF components. It also measures semantic consistency of directions, not superposition or feature spreading as such, so it is kept under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is essentially correct. The authors report that evidence supports predictions 1 (monosemantic polytope regions; directions not generally monosemantic) and 2 (polytope boundaries track semantic boundaries), and only partially supports prediction 3. They are uncertain whether the polytope lens is worth its cost, since it does not yet yield decomposable features. They suggest combining overcomplete bases with polytopes.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proposes and evaluates polytope-lens analyses; it does not reproduce the toy-model superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: Polytope-density differences vary with network training status and layer; the scaling analysis reports a density peak toward the origin and class changes at large activation magnitudes.

fits_no_version.finding: HDBSCAN clusters of activations and of binarized spline codes in GPT2-small and InceptionV1 are described as mostly monosemantic.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Small regions of activation or spline-code space in ReLU-type networks are semantically coherent.

fits_no_version.finding: In GPT2-small layer 4, 64 NMF directions appear largely monosemantic while neuron basis directions appear highly polysemantic (qualitative).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Non-basis directions found by dimensionality reduction can be more monosemantic than individual neurons in GPT2-small.

fits_no_version.finding: In trained InceptionV1, normalized polytope-boundary density is lower within a class than between classes. The gap is small but significant, grows in higher layers, and is absent in the untrained network.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Polytope boundaries are denser between semantic classes in trained image classifiers.

fits_no_version.finding: When an activation is scaled, polytope density peaks between the vector and the origin, yet class changes also occur at large magnitudes where density is low.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Polytope density marks only the inner bound of a direction's validity range.

record.problems: The paper itself notes that the intra- versus inter-class density difference is small, despite statistical significance. Several findings are qualitative or conveyed through figures without numerical values. The scaling result only partially matches the prediction. The authors also note that transformer attention and smooth activations require further treatment.
record.rows_left_out: No reported results were left out. The experiments are recorded as related polytope-lens findings rather than results for any listed version.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity sweeps, near-orthogonality or feature-geometry measurements. The paper only notes that Elhage et al.'s polytopes lie in weight space, not activation space.
No test of capacity competition or of whether important features get dedicated dimensions.
No test of polysemanticity arising without capacity pressure.
No SAE or overcomplete dictionary. Feature spreading across neurons is shown only qualitatively, via 64-component NMF in one GPT2-small layer, and is not tied to superposition.
No dictionary features are trained or evaluated for completeness, stability or canonicity.

The paper argues conceptually that globally valid linear directions are leaky, but runs no test of 1-D versus multi-dimensional features. Its own NMF result suggests some directions stay coherent across polytopes.

missing.what: Appendix A: spherical interpolation between same- and different-class activations shows higher polytope density mid-path between classes, a 'relatively weak' trend over 200 interpolations per layer. This bears on no version, but rows_left_out wrongly says nothing was omitted.

record.verdict_notes: This is a preprint from Conjecture. Its superposition content is conceptual: it argues that a sparse overcomplete basis alone will not avoid nonlinearity, and it notes that clustering is equivalent to a k=1 sparse overcomplete basis. It does not cite the original source as tested. GPT2 uses GELU, so 'spline codes' there are an approximation of polytopes.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test sparse-feature storage in toy networks, overlap or near-orthogonality, sparsity-dependent transitions, or regular feature geometry.
Does not test whether capacity competition causes polysemanticity or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Does not test whether polysemanticity arises without capacity pressure or whether it is evidence for superposition.
Does not test feature spreading across neurons or SAE recovery of sparse features. It uses NMF directions and polytope clustering, not SAEs.
Does not test whether dictionary features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
Does not test whether the features involved in superposition are one-dimensional directions or multidimensional.

rows.subject: GPT2-small
rows.operation_detail: Clustered hidden-layer activations using HDBSCAN and assessed cluster semantics.

conditions.value: various MLP layers; also layer 4 in the direction comparison
random sample of The Pile test set

rows.value: The authors report that the majority of clusters found were monosemantic; examples include token-specific and semantic clusters.
rows.note: This is evidence about polytope-lens/activation clustering, not a test of the listed superposition versions.

rows.subject: GPT2-small
rows.operation_detail: Clustered binarized spline codes using HDBSCAN.

conditions.value: random sample of The Pile test set

rows.value: Examples include clusters associated with detokenization in earlier layers and higher-level semantic groupings in later layers.
rows.note: The paper reports examples and qualitative observations, not a quantified cluster-level score.

rows.subject: GPT2-small
rows.operation_detail: Compared activation-cluster labels with cosine similarities to 64 NMF components.
rows.measure: Semantic consistency of NMF directions and basis directions
rows.value: The authors say NMF directions appear largely monosemantic, while basis directions still appear highly polysemantic.
rows.note: The paper gives qualitative conclusions from plotted examples; this does not test SAE features or feature dimensionality in superposition.
rows.check: The authors state outright that NMF directions appear largely monosemantic and that basis directions appear highly polysemantic. For the finding as recorded, 'observed' is more accurate than 'partial'. The evidence is qualitative only: histogram examples in Figs 13–15, with no counts.

rows.subject: InceptionV1
rows.operation_detail: Clustered activations using HDBSCAN and inspected the corresponding image regions.
rows.value: The paper reports examples of clusters associated with particular animal types and other visual patterns.
rows.note: Examples are qualitative and are not a measurement of superposition.

rows.subject: InceptionV1
rows.operation_detail: Measured normalized polytope-boundary density between activation vectors from same-class and different-class images.

conditions.value: multiple layers; difference increases toward higher layers

rows.measure: Hamming distance between spline codes divided by Euclidean activation distance, normalized by mean density across all pairs
rows.baseline: Mean density across all pairs is the normalization reference; exact plotted values are figure-only.
rows.value: Same-class pairs have lower normalized density than different-class pairs; the difference increases in higher layers. The paper reports t(1873.3) = −14.7; p = 3.8e − 46, and notes that the difference is small.
rows.note: The text describes the direction and significance of the result; plotted values are not stated numerically.

rows.subject: InceptionV1
rows.operation_detail: Measured normalized polytope-boundary density between activation vectors from same-class and different-class images.
rows.measure: Hamming distance between spline codes divided by Euclidean activation distance, normalized by mean density across all pairs
rows.baseline: Mean density across all pairs is the normalization reference; exact plotted values are figure-only.
rows.value: The paper states that the lower same-class density is seen only for the trained network, not the untrained network.
rows.uncertainty: 99% bootstrapped confidence intervals shown; exact values not stated
rows.note: The untrained network is the control comparison.

rows.subject: InceptionV1
rows.operation_detail: Scaled hidden activation vectors and measured local polytope density alongside class logits.

conditions.value: activation vector scaled toward and away from the origin

rows.measure: Polytope density and class changes during activation scaling
rows.baseline: Unscaled activation vector; exact values are figure-only.
rows.value: Polytope density peaks between the unscaled vector and the origin. The paper also reports class changes at large magnitudes where polytope density is low.
rows.note: The authors characterize prediction 3 as only partially supported and say the distant class changes do not match its prediction.
rows.check: The state is correct. Note that the density peak toward the origin also appears for Gaussian-noise directions and is absent in untrained networks (Appendix B).

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
